editorial:
Imagine starting your day at a regular job and ending it as a mass murderer. That is exactly what happens to Marco, a young butcher who accidentally kills a taxi driver. Instead of calling for help, he panics. When his girlfriend Paula tries to do the right thing and go to the police, Marco kills her too. From there, things just spiral out of control. You get to watch him slowly turn into a monster as he kills his brother, his brother's fiancée, and even his own father just to keep his secrets safe. Since he works at a slaughterhouse, he has a very grim way of hiding the evidence, which gives the whole movie a creepy, cold feeling.

What really works here is how the tension builds up as the people around Marco start asking too many questions. The acting is solid and makes you feel the panic of the situation. While the pacing is a bit slow in the middle, the shock value is definitely there. If you like old-school thrillers that show a person losing their mind, you will love this. You should definitely look for a 4K Blu-ray to add to your physical collection for the best quality, or you can try renting it on Apple TV for a quick movie night.
endingExplained: Everything falls apart for Marco in the end. After killing his entire family and hiding them at the meat plant, his guilt and paranoia finally catch up to him. He cannot escape the horror of what he has done. He ends up getting caught and facing the consequences of his crimes. The movie wraps up by showing that no matter how much he tried to hide the bodies, the truth eventually comes out in a brutal way.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old crime movies and psychological thrillers.
